column2: ENGLISH

[university_student.GetTitledFirstName] stands before you, cap in hand, and asks leave to go to the [university.GetName]. [university_student.GetSheHeCap] wants to read law and history and the natural philosophers, to hear the great masters dispute, and to come home a learned [university_student.GetManWoman]. The masters' fees are not small, and students are known to learn a great deal besides their books.
Go, and make me proud.
I will not allow it!

You have decided to send [university_student.GetTitledFirstName] to a university, in the hope that [university_student.GetSheHe] comes home a learned [university_student.GetManWoman]. Where will you send [university_student.GetHerHim]?
To the University of Altdorf.
To the University of Nuln.
To the University of Streissen.
To the University of Praag.
To the University of Remas.
To the University of Miragliano.
To the University of Martek.
To the University of Magritta.
On second thoughts, no. [university_student.GetFirstName] stays.
Away at University
This character is studying at a university and will come home in a few years.

[university_student.GetTitledFirstName] is home from the [university.GetName], and one look is enough. [university_student.GetSheHeCap] smells of the tavern, laughs too loud and calls for wine before noon. It makes you wonder how [university_student.GetSheHe] ever passed an examination.
Damn sot.

[university_student.GetTitledFirstName] is home from the [university.GetName], and changed. [university_student.GetSheHeCap] is wiser, surer of [university_student.GetHerHis] own mind, and full of things you never knew. The masters taught [university_student.GetHerHim] well.
Welcome home, [university_student.GetFirstName]!

[university_student.GetTitledFirstName] is home from the [university.GetName] with [university_student.GetHerHis] studies finished, but they have taken a great deal out of [university_student.GetHerHim]. Too many sleepless nights over the books have left [university_student.GetHerHim] grey and joyless.
It cannot have been that hard.

[university_student.GetTitledFirstName] is home from the [university.GetName], and not alone. [university_student.GetSheHeCap] has found a spouse among the students' lodgings and brought [university_student.GetHerHis] new family home to meet you.
Each to their own.

[university_student.GetTitledFirstName] is home from the [university.GetName], dragging [university_student.GetHerHis] feet. The cities are full of fevers and the students' lodgings are full of the cities' worst. [university_student.GetSheHeCap] will need to rest a long while.
Poor child.

[university_student.GetTitledFirstName] is home from the [university.GetName] with three carts of books behind [university_student.GetHerHim] and a head full of more. [university_student.GetSheHeCap] loved every day of it, and talks of nothing else.
I doubt they will all fit in the library.

[university_student.GetTitledFirstName] is home from the [university.GetName]. Having heard some of [university_student.GetHerHis] stories of wine, dice, duels and the daughters of innkeepers, you decide a student's life must be quite something.
That's my [university_student.GetFirstName]!

[university_student.GetTitledFirstName] has done better than anyone hoped. [university_student.GetSheHeCap] is home from the [university.GetName] a master of the old sorcery of Araby, with the flames of the desert at [university_student.GetHerHis] fingertips. A scholar of such learning will bring great honour to the family.
Excellent.
A Bound Thesis
A thesis written at a university of the Old World and thought worthy of binding by its masters. The margins are full of the author's later corrections.
[university_student.GetFirstName] goes to live at the court of the §YRector§! of the university for four years.

A letter from [From.GetFirstName] in Altdorf:\n\n"The lectures are long and the masters are dull, but the city is never dull. Half the nobility of the Empire sends its children here, to be schooled and to find a good match, and I have dined with the sons of three Electors. From my window I can see the towers of the Colleges of Magic, and at night strange lights burn in them. I am well, but the capital is dear, and my purse grows light."

A letter from [From.GetFirstName] in Nuln:\n\n"The University of Nuln is older than the Empire's oldest crowns, and its masters never let us forget it. There are students here from as far away as Araby. When the Gunnery School tests its guns the whole city shakes and the ink jumps on my desk. I am learning a great deal, but the books alone cost a fortune."

A letter from [From.GetFirstName] in Streissen:\n\n"It is a small university, and the medical school is the best part of it. The town is all whitewashed houses and parks, and it is full of talk that the Averheim bailiffs would not like to hear. The masters who taught such things were turned out years ago, but the students still whisper. Do not worry, I keep my head down. I could keep it down more easily with a little more silver."

A letter from [From.GetFirstName] in Praag:\n\n"They say the stones of this city remember the Great War against Chaos, and some nights I believe it. Faces show in the walls when the lamps go out, and no student walks the old quarter alone. The masters are stern and the winters are worse. I have learned to drink kvas and to sleep with a candle burning. Please send warm clothes, or money for them."

A letter from [From.GetFirstName] in Remas:\n\n"Remas sits on its great headland above the lagoon, and its fishermen are the best in the Old World. The city is a republic, and every student here has an opinion on how a city should be ruled and shouts it in the taverns. The Elves built here before men came, and the masters take us out to measure their ruins. I have learned more law and rhetoric in a year than in all my life before. The city is very dear, and the Tileans charge a foreigner double for everything."

A letter from [From.GetFirstName] in Miragliano:\n\n"Miragliano is built on islands, with canals for streets, and it is a city of engineers. and the masters speak of the great Leonardo as though he left yesterday. I have seen machines here that the Dwarfs would envy. The fevers come up from the Blighted Marshes in summer, so I keep to my rooms and my books. The sea is salt and the rivers are miles away, so the city buys its water by the barrel. Everything costs money here, even the water."

A letter from [From.GetFirstName] in Magritta:\n\n"Every ship of the south seems to come into the Bay of Quietude, even ships from Araby. The great temple of Myrmidia, which all her temples in the Old World obey, rises over the harbour, and the masters here are as fond of the sword as of the pen. I have been taught the diestro way of fencing by a man who fights duels over the placing of a comma. The Estalians are proud and quick to take offence, so I am learning courtesy as well as letters. A gentleman's education here is not cheap."

A letter from [From.GetFirstName] in Martek:\n\n"Martek stands high in the mountains, and vultures big enough to carry off a horse circle its towers. Its scholars study the stars, and they say the fire of the heavens can be read like a book. I have seen one of them call a flame into his hand. The days are hot, the nights are cold and the copying of books never ends. The masters expect gifts from their pupils, as is the custom of Araby."
Send a purse of silver.
[From.GetSheHeCap] must learn to live within [From.GetHerHis] means.
With money to spare, [From.GetFirstName] is more likely to come home §Ybetter educated§!, but also more likely to come home a §Ydrunkard§! or a §Yhedonist§!.
Living on little, [From.GetFirstName] is more likely to come home a §Yscholar§!, but also more likely to come home §Yworn out§!.
Endow the University
Pay for new halls, books and chairs at the university of your city. Its learning will spread through your lands, and its students will come home wiser.
Endowed University
A lord has paid for new halls, books and chairs. Learning spreads faster here, and the students graduate learned more often.

A rider in your family's colours comes into the university courtyard with mud to the knees and a sealed letter. [From.GetName] is yours now, and your people need their lord more than the masters need another pupil. Your books are packed by nightfall.
My studies must wait. I am needed at home.
University of Talabheim
University of Salzenmund
University of Marienburg
To the University of Talabheim.
To the University of Salzenmund.
To the University of Marienburg.
To the University of Kufra.

A letter from [From.GetFirstName] in Talabheim:\n\n"The city lies inside a great crater in the heart of the Great Forest, and from the rim you can see the whole of it, fields and temples and all, walled in by stone that no army has ever climbed. The universities here are for young nobles, and most of my fellows study the wine of the taverns and the ladies of the city more than their books. I try to be the exception. It is not cheap to be the exception."

A letter from [From.GetFirstName] in Salzenmund:\n\n"Salzenmund is a free town and proud of it, and the university is the newest thing in it. The masters of sciences here are bold men who say the world can be understood, and the old priests mutter about them. West of the town lies the Laurelorn, and the Elves who keep it do not like visitors. The woollens are good and the cheese is better, but books must come all the way from Altdorf, and they cost accordingly."

A letter from [From.GetFirstName] in Marienburg:\n\n"There is no city like Marienburg. Ships from every shore crowd the harbour, the Burgomeisters answer to no Emperor, and the great temple of Manann, which all his temples obey, stands over the docks. The university was founded by merchants and its masters think like merchants. Every lecture has a price, and so does every book, every candle and every friend."

A letter from [From.GetFirstName] in Kufra:\n\n"The caravans come into Kufra out of the desert, and with them come scholars from every city of Araby. The masters teach the stars, the laws of the Sultans and the arts of numbers, and they dispute each other in the courtyards until the call to evening prayer. Water and paper are dear here, and a scholar is expected to pay well for both."
Found the University of Salzenmund
Salzenmund is a free town of learned men with no university to teach them. Pay for the halls and the first chairs, and the young nobles of the north will no longer have to go to Altdorf to study.
Found the University of Marienburg

The merchants of Marienburg have money, ships and the trade of the whole world, but no university. Pay for the halls and the first chairs, and the city will school the sons and daughters of the Wasteland, the north of the Empire and even of Bretonnia.
The university is founded, a §YRector§! takes the chair and it begins to take students.
